thought_title: Welcome the bishop as the Sender

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Καὶ ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω: πάντα γάρ, ὃν πέμπει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἰς ἰδίαν οἰκονομίαν, οὕτως δεῖ ἡμᾶς αὐτὸν δέχεσθαι, ὡς αὐτὸν τὸν πέμψαντα, τὸν οὖν ἐπίσκοπον δῆλον ὅτι ὡς αὐτὸν κύριον δεῖ προσβλέπειν. [2] αὐτὸς μὲν οὖν Ὀνήσιμος ὑπερεπαινεῖ ὑμῶν τὴν ἐν θεῷ εὐταξίαν, ὅτι πάντες κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ζῆτε καὶ ὅτι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεμία αἵρεσις κατοικεῖ: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: And the more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him fear him. For everyone whom the master of the house sends to manage his own household, we must receive in the same way as the one who sent him. So it is clear that we must look on the bishop as the Lord himself. Now Onesimus himself highly praises your good order in God: that you all live according to the truth, and that no faction has a home among you; in fact you do not even listen to anyone beyond one who speaks truthfully about Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: The more silent you find a bishop, the more you should stand in awe of him. Whoever the Master of the house sends to run his household, we must welcome as we would welcome the one who sent him (Matthew 10:40; John 13:20). Plainly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself.

Onesimus himself warmly praises your good order in God. You all live by the truth, and no faction makes its home among you. Indeed, you will not listen to anyone at all unless he speaks truly about Jesus Christ.

choices.term: ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω
choices.english: The more silent you find a bishop, the more you should stand in awe of him
choices.why: φοβέομαι here is reverent fear; Ignatius defends a quiet bishop against those who despise his silence.
In Ignatius αἵρεσις is still a party or split; 'heresy' imports a later technical sense.

choices.term: οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ
choices.english: you will not listen to anyone at all unless he speaks truly about Jesus Christ
choices.why: περί + genitive makes Jesus Christ the subject matter of the speaker, not the speaker.
rejected: rather than to Jesus Christ speaking in truth (ANF; misreads περί)

anf_compare.notes: ANF ends 'Nor do you hearken to any one rather than to Jesus Christ speaking in truth', making Christ the speaker. The Greek τινος ... περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος means a person speaking about Jesus Christ. ANF 'to be over His household' and 'no sect' are otherwise close.

bible_refs.note: ὁ δεχόμενος ... δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με: receiving the one sent as the sender
receiving whomever I send receives the one who sent me (τὸν πέμψαντά με)

notes: Whole chapter 6 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
ANF marks Matthew 24:45 (the household steward); the οἰκοδεσπότης image fits Gospel parables generally but no single verse matches. Not inline.

review.notes: Locked paragraph [1] is Ephesians 6.1–2: ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω; receive the envoy ὡς αὐτὸν τὸν πέμψαντα; regard the bishop ὡς αὐτὸν κύριον; Onesimus praises εὐταξίαν; then ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ. Pass A keeps the indefinite observer and the present comparative. Pass B contradicts both with second-person awe and a future exclusive condition. Matthew 10:40 and John 13:20 match the supplied bible_refs for the reception wording and are not a wrong citation. Connectives Καί/γάρ and warmly/highly are not the fail.
reasons: Agency: Locked Greek 'ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω' has τις seeing and third-person φοβείσθω; Pass A has 'the more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him fear him'; Pass B contradicts both with 'The more silent you find a bishop, the more you should stand in awe of him'.

Negation and modality: Locked Greek 'ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ' is present and comparative (πλέον ἢ); Pass A 'you do not even listen to anyone beyond one who speaks truthfully about Jesus Christ' preserves that; Pass B 'you will not listen to anyone at all unless he speaks truly about Jesus Christ' widens the denial, adds 'at all' and 'unless', and shifts ἀκούετε to future 'will'.

review.notes: Paragraph 1: Locked Greek matches source identity (Ignatius Ephesians 6). Completeness: all clauses translated in Pass A and B. Negation: 'οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον' correctly rendered as 'you will not listen to anyone at all unless' in B (Pass A omits 'at all' but sense preserved). Agency: 'ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ... πέμπει' (master sends) preserved; 'πέμψαντα' (the one who sent) correctly attributed. Modality: 'δεῖ' (must) consistently rendered. Doctrine: bishop as Lord's representative upheld. Scripture: Pass B adds Matthew 10:40 and John 13:20 as gloss; these are correct per notes and lemmas, and Pass A lacks them but they are additions not contradictions. Title: 'Welcome the bishop as the Sender' names the thought (receiving the bishop as receiving the Sender). Notes disclose OCR/variants status. Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties.
